newsitem.title: USA: Salomon, Alex.Brown quarterly earnings down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Salomon, Alex.Brown quarterly earnings down sharply.

text.p: Brokerage firms Salomon Inc. and Alex. Brown Inc. reported sharply lower second-quarter earnings Thursday, hit by broad declines in investment banking revenues.
Salomon said profits fell by 24 percent to $220 million vs. $291 million in the same year-ago period. Earnings per share fell to $1.89 from $2.58 a year ago.

Global investment banking revenues totalled $221 million during the second quarter, essentially unchanged from the 1997 first quarter but down from the record revenues of $251 million in the second quarter of 1996.

Fixed-income sales and trading net revenues fell to $532 million from $706 million in the second quarter of 1996. The company said the decrease reflected lower revenues in both proprietary trading and customer sales and trading.
Asset management revenues were $20 million for the period, nearly double the $11 million recorded in the second quarter of 1996.
Salomon also said it completed the sale of Basis Petroleum to Valero Energy Corp on May 1.
Baltimore-based Alex. Brown said its net income fell 36 percent to $31.7 million from $49.8 million a year ago. Earnings per share fell to $1.23 from $2.01 in last year's second quarter.
Current second-quarter earnings included a charge related to severance costs which reduced primary earnings by 18 cents a share, the company said.
Investment banking revenues fell 29 percent to $95.5 million in the second quarter, primarily due to diminished underwriting activity in the equity offerings market, the company said.
Merger and advisory revenues totalled $39 million in the period, up 66 percent from $23 million in the second quarter of 1996.
The company said it would hold a special meeting of shareholders Aug. 13 to consider a proposal to approve a merger agreement, announced in April, between Alex. Brown and Bankers Trust New York Corp.
Salomon stock rose $1.69 to $56.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading. Alex. Brown was up 37.5 cents at $77.94 a share, also on NYSE.
